concepts.def: IBDP Music 2020 syllabus organises study around four areas: music for sociocultural and political expression, for listening and performance, for dramatic impact, presentation, entertainment.
Personal or community traditions students draw on; required as first lens for global comparison in the exploring component.
Coursework requires study of at least four musical contexts; cannot be from same geographical/cultural cluster.
Bruno Nettl's Study of Ethnomusicology 1983 framed music in cultural context as central; Nettl identified 29 issues for the field.
Cross-cultural exchange spans Silk Road via Marco Polo (1271-95), West African to Caribbean (transatlantic), Beatles to Indian classical (1965 Norwegian Wood).
Coined 1987 at London meeting of independent labels (Globestyle, Cooking Vinyl); marketing category for non-Western traditions.

concepts.def: IBDP Music portfolio task; create musical material through composing, arranging, improvising or producing across multiple contexts.
Sketching motifs, harmonic experiments, orchestration trials and revision drafts documented in commentary; Beethoven's sketchbooks model practice.
Reharmonisation, reorchestration, metric modulation; Quincy Jones's arrangement of Fly Me to the Moon for Sinatra 1964 exemplary.
Spontaneous composition within structure; jazz blues changes and Indian classical alap demonstrate improvised disciplines.
Multitrack recording (Les Paul 1947), MIDI 1983, Pro Tools 1991, plugin synthesis; transformed music creation in studios.
Standard staff notation, lead sheets, tablature, graphic scores (Cornelius Cardew's Treatise 1967), DAW MIDI clips for the digital domain.

concepts.def: IBDP Music final assessment for performance includes solo/ensemble recording, programme notes and reflective commentary linking to inquiry areas.
Historically informed performance (HIP) Nikolaus Harnoncourt 1953 Concentus Musicus Wien revived Baroque techniques.
Curatorial decisions about repertoire order; Joseph Joachim's chronological format in Berlin 1864 influenced modern recitals.
Visual, gestural and ritual elements; Glenn Gould's elimination of live concerts 1964 highlighted recording vs concert distinction.
Intonation, dynamic balance, articulation, vibrato control; assessed against stylistic criteria for chosen contexts.
Christopher Small's Musicking 1998 reframed performance as a relational social act including listeners.

Davis's Kind of Blue March 1959 based on modes rather than chord changes; John Coltrane's Giant Steps 1959 contrasting approach.
Ornette Coleman's Free Jazz: A Collective Improvisation 1960; abandoned fixed harmony; Cecil Taylor, Albert Ayler, Art Ensemble of Chicago.

concepts.def: Gregorian chant codified 9th-10th C; Hildegard of Bingen (1098-1179); Josquin des Prez (1450-1521) and Palestrina (1525-94) polyphony peak.
Monteverdi's Orfeo 1607 first major opera; figured bass; Bach Brandenburg Concertos 1721, Handel Messiah 1741, Vivaldi Four Seasons 1725.
Haydn (symphony father, 104 symphonies), Mozart (operas, K.626 Requiem 1791), Beethoven (9 symphonies 1800-24); sonata form.
Berlioz Symphonie Fantastique 1830, Wagner Tristan 1865 with Tristan chord, Brahms 4 symphonies, Mahler 9 finished symphonies.
Debussy's Prelude a l'Apres-midi d'un faune 1894 and La Mer 1905; Ravel's Bolero 1928; influenced by Symbolist poets and gamelan.
Schoenberg's atonality 1908 (George Songs); Stravinsky's Rite of Spring 1913 Paris premiere riot; Webern, Berg complete Second Viennese School.

concepts.def: Indonesian percussion orchestra of bronze gongs, metallophones, drums (kendhang) and bamboo flutes (suling); Javanese and Balinese traditions distinct.
Two principal Javanese tuning systems; slendro pentatonic, pelog heptatonic; tuning unique to each gamelan set.
Yogyakarta and Surakarta kraton ensembles; refined court style with vocal singers (pesinden) and rebab fiddle.
Developed c.1915 in North Bali; faster, more virtuosic than Javanese gamelan; I Wayan Beratha leading composer.
Cyclical timekeeping marked by large gongs (gong ageng), kethuk and kempul; nested colotomic levels in gendhing forms.
Debussy heard gamelan at 1889 Paris Exposition; influenced Pagodes 1903; Britten studied gamelan during 1956 Bali visit.

concepts.def: Melodic framework with characteristic ascending (aroha) and descending (avaroha) scales, signature phrases (pakad) and mood (rasa).
North Indian Hindustani gharanas (Gwalior, Kirana); South Indian Carnatic tradition codified by trinity Tyagaraja, Muttuswami Dikshitar, Syama Sastri (early 19th C).
Cyclic rhythmic framework; common talas teental (16 beats), jhaptal (10), rupak (7); marked by claps and waves.
Hindustani khyal opens with unmetered alap, progresses to vilambit (slow) and drut (fast) compositions in chosen raga and tala.
Sitar (modernised by Ravi Shankar), tabla (Zakir Hussain), sarod (Ali Akbar Khan), bansuri flute (Hariprasad Chaurasia), vocal.
Composed kriti forms (Tyagaraja's Pancharatna); RTP showcases improvisation of ragam alapana, tanam exposition and pallavi line.

concepts.def: Goblet-shaped Malinke drum from Mali, Guinea, Burkina Faso c.13th C Mali Empire; played with bare hands; lead with dunun bass drums.
Multiple metric streams interlocking; A M Jones documented 1959 in Studies in African Music; 3-against-2 hemiola fundamental.
Talking drums of Nigeria; tension cords vary pitch to mimic tonal speech; ensemble leader (iya ilu) plays praise verses.
Ghanaian war dance ensemble; gankogui bell, axatse rattle, kidi and sogo drums, lead atsimevu; documented by C K Ladzekpo and Hewitt Pantaleoni.
Shona thumb piano of Zimbabwe; sacred bira ceremony invokes ancestors; Paul Berliner's Soul of Mbira 1978 the seminal study.
African drumming roots in samba (Brazil), bata (Yoruba-Cuban), candomble (Bahia), rumba (Cuba), bomba (Puerto Rico).

Piano Phase 1967 uses two pianos drifting out of sync; It's Gonna Rain 1965 tape phasing; Drumming 1971 1.5-hour work.

concepts.def: Twelve-tone technique announced 1923; tone row uses all twelve chromatic pitches once before repetition; Suite for Piano Op 25 first.
Prime, retrograde, inversion, retrograde-inversion forms; matrix permutation provides 48 row variants.
Schoenberg with Alban Berg and Anton Webern; expressionism then dodecaphony; Berg's Lyric Suite 1926 and Webern's Op 21 Symphony 1928.
Olivier Messiaen's Mode de valeurs 1949 extended serialism to rhythm and dynamics; Boulez's Structures Ia 1952 and Stockhausen Kreuzspiel 1951.
Internationale Ferienkurse fur Neue Musik attracted Boulez, Stockhausen, Nono, Maderna; postwar avant-garde nexus.
Babbitt's Who Cares If You Listen 1958 defended; Penderecki, Crumb broke from strict serialism; minimalism reaction emerged.

concepts.def: Beethoven Symphony No 5 1808 four-note motif transformed across movements; influenced cyclic forms in Berlioz, Liszt, Franck.
Functional harmony (Rameau Traite 1722), modal (jazz), chromaticism (Wagner), polytonality (Stravinsky), atonality (Schoenberg).
Multiple independent voices; species counterpoint codified Fux Gradus ad Parnassum 1725; Bach Art of Fugue 1740s peak.
Berlioz Treatise on Instrumentation 1844 (revised by Strauss 1904); colour and balance choices defining sonority.
Binary, ternary, rondo, sonata-allegro, theme and variations (Bach Goldberg 1741, Brahms Op 24 1861), through-composed.
Monophonic (chant), homophonic (Mozart's Eine kleine Nachtmusik 1787), polyphonic (Palestrina), heterophonic (gamelan).

concepts.def: 1950s onwards; period instruments, original tunings (A=415 for Baroque), ornamentation tables; Nikolaus Harnoncourt and Concentus Musicus pioneers.
Chopin's tempo rubato in Rondo Op 5 1828 directed flexible time within constant accompaniment; Liszt extended interpretive freedom.
Baroque appoggiaturas, trills, mordents and turns; C P E Bach Essay on True Art 1753 the authoritative period guide.
Just intonation, meantone, well-tempered (Werckmeister 1691), equal temperament (standard since 19th C); Bach Well-Tempered Clavier 1722/42 24 keys.
Continuous vibrato unfashionable before 1900; HIP performers like Roger Norrington advocate minimal vibrato in Beethoven and earlier.
Czerny-Liszt-Boulanger lineage in piano; Auer to Heifetz in violin; lineages shape interpretive traditions.

concepts.def: Heinrich Schenker's Der freie Satz 1935; reductive analysis revealing Ursatz background, middleground and foreground.
Allen Forte's Structure of Atonal Music 1973 catalogued unordered pitch-class sets in atonal works; prime forms and interval vectors.
William Caplin's Classical Form 1998 categorises beginning-middle-end thematic functions in sonata-form themes.
David Lewin's Generalized Musical Intervals 1987 and Richard Cohn 1996; PLR transformations track chromatic chord relations.
Leonard Ratner's Classic Music 1980 catalogued late-18th-century topoi (military, pastoral, sturm und drang) as semantic markers.
Eric Clarke's Ways of Listening 2005 and CHARM project Mazurka analyses since 2004; empirical study of recorded performances.
